A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet. Everything you send goes through that tunnel in scrambled form, so people in between can't read it.

Here is how it goes:

Your device scrambles your traffic before it leaves.
It travels to the VPN company's computer, which unscrambles it.
That computer then visits the website for you, so the site sees the VPN's address instead of yours.

This helps on public Wi-Fi, since others on the network can't snoop. It also hides your location from websites. It does not make you fully anonymous, because the VPN company can still see your activity.
